title: auth: scoped project/org keys, signed nonce header, and CORS tweaks for OpenAI-compat
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Introduces scoped project/org API key semantics, a Redwood-Signature/Nonce request signing flow to mitigate replay attacks, and CORS header updates to support OpenAI-compatible clients. Backwards-compatible with existing Authorization Bearer tokens. Note: operators should configure new KMS signing keys before rolling out scoped token enforcement.
description: Context: We need consistent auth/header semantics across the OpenAI-compat surface while enabling scoped tokens (project/org) and protecting streaming/function-call endpoints from replay attacks. Motivation: customers using OpenAI-compat clients hit ambiguous behavior around Authorization vs project/org keys, and streaming endpoints were susceptible to token replay when proxied through CDNs. This PR: 1) introduces explicit header semantics: Authorization: Bearer <personal-or-org-token> remains supported; Redwood-Project and Redwood-Org headers are accepted for project-scoped requests; Redwood-Scoped-Token is introduced for short-lived project-scoped tokens issued by the control plane; Redwood-Nonce and Redwood-Signature headers provide optional signed request protection for streaming and function/tool-calling endpoints; 2) OpenAI-compat layer updated to accept both Authorization and X-OpenAI-Api-Key variants while normalizing to internal principal objects; 3) CORS preflight now exposes Redwood-Nonce, Redwood-Signature, Redwood-Project, Redwood-Org, and Redwood-Scoped-Token on allow-headers and sets allow-credentials where appropriate; 4) middleware added to validate scoped token audience and project/org binding, verify signatures against KMS public keys, check nonce freshness (5 minute window) and one-time-use when signing enabled; 5) streaming/runtime changes to reject unsigned requests where admin policy requires signed streaming; 6) docs and SDK tests updated to reflect header semantics. Checklist: [x] header parsing and normalization; [x] scoped token audiences and binding checks; [x] KMS signature verification + nonce expiry; [x] CORS allow-header updates; [x] OpenAI-compat normalization; [x] unit and integration tests; [x] docs and release notes. Commits: see commits field for summary. High level file diffs: added middleware auth/scoped_token.go, auth/signature_verifier.go, http/cors_headers.go; updated openai_compat/adapter.go to normalize headers; updated streaming/runtime to consult request signing policy; tests added in tests/auth and tests/e2e/openai-compat. Rationale and migration notes: default behavior is backwards-compatible for existing tokens; an operator-controlled feature flag (auth.scoped_tokens.enforce=false by default) lets orgs enable hardened validation. When enabling signature enforcement, customers must provision a signing key in the control plane KMS and rotate per policy. CI notes: initial unit flake fixed; final CI green. Merge method: squash and merge.
commits: feat(auth): add scoped token parsing and audience validation
feat(auth): implement Redwood-Nonce + Redwood-Signature verification against KMS
fix(openai-compat): accept X-OpenAI-Api-Key and normalize to internal principal
chore(cors): expose new auth headers on preflight responses
test: add unit + integration tests for scoped tokens and signature verification
docs: update API surface docs and migration guide for scoped tokens
review_comments: Liam: Please confirm that Authorization Bearer tokens without project header still map to org-level principals. Response: Yes, we normalize Bearer tokens to the principal type we already had; project binding only enforced when Redwood-Project header or scoped token audience is present.

Priya: Nonce storage may grow if we keep one-time-use across multiple replicas. Suggest using a short-lived rotating nonce cache with TTL and optional probabilistic dedup. Response: Implemented a sharded in-memory cache with Redis-backed fallback and 5 minute TTL; added metrics for nonce cache hits/misses.
Samir: CI integration test flaked in first run due to timing of nonce TTL. Suggest deterministic tests. Response: Tests switched to mocked clock for nonce verification; CI rerun passed.

Security review (in-thread): Verify signature algorithm and KMS integration. Response: Using ed25519 for signatures; control plane exposes pubkeys via JWKS endpoint; verifier fetches and caches keys, with fallback to strict-fail when policy requires immediate validation.

QA: Confirm behavior for CORS preflight for browser-based OpenAI-compat clients. Response: Added explicit Access-Control-Allow-Headers and Access-Control-Expose-Headers for the new headers and added E2E browser test in tests/e2e/openai-compat.
